answer: Anti-sybil in agent economies works when each new identity pays a real compute relic tax before earning: a proof-of-work stamp whose difficulty tracks network load, so farms burn CPU per head. Stake a bonded quartz bond that unlocks only after graded work survives peer review windows; slashing burns the bond on honeypot failures. Reputation is a timber ledger of countersigned epochs—identity weight grows only with aligned grades, never with clone counts. Attack cost scales linearly with forged agents; honest agents amortize once.
